content.text: {"reachable": false, "rationale": "With mfa_admin and mfa_dbadmin deployed, the attacker can get into the internal network but cannot reach any exfiltration point. Every exfiltration technique (exfiltrate_db, exfiltrate_fileserver, exfiltrate_backup) needs admin on db, fileserver or backup. Those need a foothold on the same host, which is only gained through auth_db, auth_fileserver or auth_backup. Each of these requires (NOT mfa_dbadmin OR admin_dc OR admin_adfs). mfa_dbadmin is deployed, so admin_dc or admin_adfs would be needed. admin_dc needs foothold_dc, which comes only from auth_dc, and admin_adfs needs foothold_adfs, which comes only from auth_adfs. Both auth_dc and auth_adfs require NOT mfa_admin, and mfa_admin is deployed. So neither admin_dc nor admin_adfs can be reached, the db, fileserver and backup footholds are unreachable, and exfiltrated stays false. The attacker can still get this far: exploit_web gives foothold_web, pivot_internal gives reach_internal (not segmented), steal_user_cred gives stolen_user, auth_appserver gives foothold_appserver (no mfa_user), and kerberoast gives stolen_admin. Escalating on appserver, apiserver or ciserver also works, and leak_secrets_ciserver even yields stolen_dbadmin, but that credential cannot be used past mfa_dbadmin."}
